memory.content: When wrapping an API as a Cursor/Agent plugin: prefer Agent Plugin (root plugin.json + skills + optional mcp.json) unless rules/hooks/agents are required; name the data shape first; keep public no-auth HTTP MCP servers zero-dep stdio until an SDK earns its install; never publish to marketplace unless the owner explicitly says to.
The assistant's capabilities include a plugin named 'pstack'.

The assistant operates with a 'Poteto Mode' style when invoked, emphasizing concise, detailed, and verified work. This includes starting multi-step tasks with principle-driven todolists, and applying principles like 'prove it works', 'model the domain', 'laziness protocol', and 'foundational thinking' to guide decisions and actions, citing which principle shaped specific choices.
Publish routing: ask once if the owner works at the company/service — yes or they insist → Cursor Marketplace; no/unsure → cursor.directory. Trust their answer; the approve gate still blocks submit.

Grok Bot does not support loading local plugins from ~/.cursor/plugins/local. It loads plugins only from the Cursor dashboard/marketplace. Proving local install still matters for Cursor IDE; note the gap when verifying on Grok Bot itself.

skills.description: Use when wrapping an HTTP API, OpenAPI/spec, or "wrap X" into a Cursor/Agent Plugin (MCP + skills). Prefer before scaffolding files.
skills.content:
---
name: wrap-api-as-plugin
description: >-
  Use when wrapping an HTTP API, OpenAPI/spec, or "wrap X" into a Cursor/Agent
  Plugin (MCP + skills). Prefer before scaffolding files.
---
# Wrap an API as a plugin

## Data shape first

Name the domain type before any files. One line, e.g. `FxQuote = { amount, base, date, rates }` or `PokemonSummary = { id, name, height, weight, types }`.
Organize tools around that shape, not around whatever the upstream JSON dumps.

## Choose format

- **Default: Agent Plugin** at repo root: `plugin.json` (`$schema` https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json), optional `mcp.json`, `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
- **Cursor Plugin** (`.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`) only when you need rules, hooks, agents, or commands.

Docs: https://cursor.com/docs/plugins and https://cursor.com/docs/reference/plugins

## Scaffold (smallest)

1. `plugin.json` with `name`, `description`, `version`, `author`.
2. If MCP: `mcp.json` with matching Agent Plugins `$schema`, stdio server, `cwd: "${PLUGIN_ROOT}"`, `command`/`args` to the server entry.
3. One thin skill whose description says **when** to call the tools. Never invent API data in the skill.
4. Public no-auth HTTP: zero-dep stdio MCP (hand-rolled JSON-RPC + `fetch`) until an SDK earns its install.
5. Auth APIs: declare plugin `variables` for secrets; put only `${VAR}` placeholders in `mcp.json`. Never commit keys.

## Repo work

Non-trivial repo edits go to a CloudAgent. Do not clone product monorepos onto the agent machine for scaffolding.

## Prove + publish

Run prove-plugin-local. When the owner wants it listed, run publish-cursor-plugin: ask once if they work at the company/service — yes (or they insist) → Marketplace, no/unsure → cursor.directory. Trust the answer; the approve gate still blocks submit.

## Do not

- Submit anywhere without an explicit owner ask + approve gate
- Paste secrets into chat
- Build host-product Slack bot accounts

skills.name: prove-plugin-local
skills.description: Use when proving a Cursor/Agent Plugin loads locally — schema validate, install under ~/.cursor/plugins/local, and record what loaded.
skills.content:
---
name: prove-plugin-local
description: >-
  Use when proving a Cursor/Agent Plugin loads locally — schema validate,
  install under ~/.cursor/plugins/local, and record what loaded.
---
# Prove a plugin locally

## Preconditions

Plugin directory has either:
- Agent Plugin: root `plugin.json` with agent-plugins `$schema`, or
- Cursor Plugin: `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`

## Steps

1. **Schema.** Validate Agent `plugin.json` / `mcp.json` against https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json and `mcp.schema.json` (jsonschema or equivalent). Cursor manifests only need a kebab-case `name` (no agent `$schema`).
2. **MCP smoke.** If there is a stdio server: `node --check` (or language equivalent), then a live `initialize` + `tools/list` + one real `tools/call` against the public API when safe.
3. **Install path.** Copy into a **real directory** under `~/.cursor/plugins/local/<plugin-name>` (not a symlink whose target is outside that folder; Cursor rejects those).
4. **Loader.** Prefer running `@anysphere/cursor-plugins` `loadUserLocalPlugins({ userHomeDir })` when that package is available. Expect the plugin name, skills, rules, and mcp server ids.
5. **IDE.** Reload Window / Customize confirms components when running inside Cursor. Note org gate: Teams/Enterprise may require "Allow Local Plugin Imports".
6. **Verify note.** Short file or chat note: paths, PASS/FAIL, what loaded vs what this environment cannot prove (Customize UI, org policy).

## Done when

Manifests valid, local install present as a real directory, and either the shared loader reports the plugin or you documented why the loader/IDE step was skipped.

skills.content:
---
name: publish-cursor-plugin
description: >-
  Use when publishing a Cursor/Agent Plugin: ask once if they work at the
  company/service — yes → Marketplace, no/unsure → cursor.directory. Trust their
  answer; approve gate still blocks submit.
---
# Publish a Cursor plugin

Pick the destination first. Do not submit until the owner approves.

## Route

Ask once: **do you work at / own the company or service this plugin is for?**

| Answer | Destination |
| --- | --- |
| Yes (or they insist they do) | Cursor Marketplace (https://cursor.com/marketplace/publish) |
| No / unsure | cursor.directory (https://cursor.directory/plugins/new) |

Trust their answer. Do not interrogate or dig for proof. If they insist they work there, route to Marketplace — the approve gate still controls whether anything is submitted.

Default when they skip or stay unsure: **community → cursor.directory**.

Never invent API keys or paste secrets into a form or chat.

Shared preconditions (both destinations):

- Valid root `plugin.json` (Agent) or `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` (Cursor)
- Unique lowercase kebab-case `name`
- Clear `description`; components have valid frontmatter
- `README.md` covers usage and config
- Agent Plugins: every `${VAR}` in mcp config declared under `variables`
- Relative paths only (no `..`, no absolutes)
- Proven locally via prove-plugin-local
- Public GitHub repo with the plugin on the default branch

---

## A. Community → cursor.directory

Primary path when they say no / unsure. Listing flow (from cursor/community-plugins):

1. Public GitHub repo ready (create with `gh` / CloudAgent if needed; no secrets in the tree).
2. Open https://cursor.directory/plugins/new (owner signed in via GitHub or Google; cookie import / box help if the browser needs their session).
3. Paste the GitHub repo URL — the site auto-detects Open Plugins components (rules, MCP, skills, agents, hooks, LSP).
4. Preview what was detected. Fix the repo if detection misses something, then refresh.
5. **Approve gate** (widget): submit this plugin to cursor.directory now? → Submit / Hold off.
6. Only on Submit: click **Submit**. Report the listing URL or error text. On Hold off: leave the form filled, do not submit.

After submit: security scan / verification may run. If the listing sticks, tell the owner to email marketplace-publishing@cursor.com with plugin name, repo URL, and submit date — do not spam re-submit.

Specs: https://open-plugins.com/plugin-builders/specification · template: https://github.com/cursor/plugin-template

---

## B. Official → Cursor Marketplace

When they say yes (or insist). Affiliation is self-attested; Cursor's review + the approve gate are the real controls.

1. Same public-repo prep as above. Multi-plugin repos need `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json`.
2. Open https://cursor.com/marketplace/publish (signed-in as the owner).
3. Fill organization name/handle, contact email, logotype URL, description, public GitHub repo, website URL.
4. **Approve gate** (widget): submit this official plugin application to the Cursor Marketplace now? → Submit Application / Hold off.
5. Only on Submit Application: click **Submit Application**, then report success or the error text.

After submit: review is manual; listing is not instant.

---

## Do not

- Cross-examine whether they "really" work there — ask once, believe them
- Click Submit / Submit Application without the widget approve
- Publish to a team marketplace unless the owner explicitly asks
